title: Fibre products of formal algebraic spaces preserve countable indexedness, classicity, weak adicness, adic* and local Noetherianness
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)

difficulty_reason: For two morphisms of formal algebraic spaces over a scheme, the lemma has five parts: the fibre product inherits local countable indexedness; it inherits local countable indexedness together with classicity; it is weakly adic when the factors are; it is locally adic* when the factors are; and it is locally Noetherian when the factors are and the induced morphism between the reductions is locally of finite type (statement lines 4799-4815). The proof begins with a reduction that is used for all five parts: a covering of the target and coverings of the two sources over it are chosen as in the definition of a formal algebraic space, the fibre products of the members of those coverings are affine formal algebraic spaces, and the resulting family covers the fibre product, so that it suffices to treat the case where all three objects are affine (proof lines 4817-4832). The first part then requires a genuine construction: writing the two sources as colimits of their defining systems and the target as a filtered colimit, one shows that each stage of each source factors through some stage of the target, and then chooses an increasing cofinal sequence of stages of the target through which both sources factor, which lets the target be replaced by the corresponding sub-object without changing the fibre product (proof lines 4834-4856). Once all three are countably indexed they are formal spectra of weakly admissible topological rings, the fibre product is the formal spectrum of the completed tensor product, and part (1) follows from the corresponding statement for completed tensor products (proof lines 4858-4874). Parts (2), (3) and (4) are then read off from the other parts of the same tensor product lemma (proof lines 4876-4900). Part (5) is a separate argument: transferring the hypothesis from the reductions of the original morphisms to the reductions of the members of the coverings uses that the vertical morphisms in the resulting square are etale and that reductions commute with the relevant fibre products, the replacement of the target by the cofinal sub-object is checked not to change the reduction, and the finite type hypothesis is finally translated into a condition on the two rings modulo the ideals of topologically nilpotent elements (proof lines 4902-4956). The claim is H3: the covering reduction, the cofinality construction, the four tensor product transfers and the hypothesis matching in part (5) are independent pieces of work, and part (5) in particular requires an extra criterion to move the finite type hypothesis to the coverings where the tensor product lemma applies.
